Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curves $y= 2^x,$ $y=\sqrt{x}$  and lines $x=0$ and $y=2,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of a function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/b80527fdef6f890581b8f56431e1b72a8f7eae3b41827caa16486ed9f2fd45ea.png)

source.question: e-7198
source.value:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions $D_1$ and $D_2,$ as shown below.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/939e46b3ed4266f3c18d3567f951276e420292781cfc414711c244f453bc4029.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
D_1 = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x  \leq 1, \quad \sqrt x \leq y \leq 2^x \big\}
$$

and 

$$
D_2 = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq x  \leq 4, \quad \sqrt x \leq y \leq 2 \big\}.
$$

 

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{{2}^{x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-7199
source.value:
First, notice that:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2+\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,x={e}^{y-2}\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions $D_1$ and $D_2,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/2228ad860fea1e2c30d20bce749f654da02a97c65fd5e70152a07761e26f3e78.png)

    

As a result, we get

$$
D_1 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq y  \leq 2, \quad 1 \leq x \leq e \bigg\}
$$

and 

$$
D_2 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 2 \leq y  \leq 3, \quad e^{y-2} \leq x \leq e\bigg\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{{e}^{y-2}}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions $D_1$ and $D_2,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/6812e8036df171e162bee49d2edcff6d4a742e7bb4f14247713bd2332c64ccc6.png)

 

As a result, we get

$$
D_1 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: -2 \leq y  \leq 0, \quad 0 \leq x \leq y^3\!-\!4y \bigg\}
$$

and 

$$
D_2 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y  \leq 1, \quad 2y^3\!-\!2y \leq x \leq 0 \bigg\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{3}-4y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2{y}^{3}-2y}^{0}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}[x]_{0}^{{y}^{3}-4y}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{2{y}^{3}-2y}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}({y}^{3}-4y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}(2y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}-2{y}^{2}]}_{-2}^{0}+{[{y}^{2}-\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
